title: Rajamouli's Varanasi Will Be the First Non-English Film Shot Entirely in IMAX
excerpt: The director of RRR and Baahubali is betting Rs 1,000 crore on a time-travel epic starring Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, and Prithviraj Sukumaran, with Hollywood VFX studios and a motion capture facility built from scratch.
body:
• SS Rajamouli's Varanasi, starring Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, and Prithviraj Sukumaran, will be the first non-English film shot entirely in the 1.43:1 IMAX format.
  • The film is a time-travel epic drawing from Hindu mythology, including sequences inspired by the Ramayana, with a reported budget of Rs 1,000 crore.
  • Three major international VFX studios — Cinesite, Trixter, and Assemblage Entertainment — are working on the film, alongside a state-of-the-art motion capture facility built at Annapurna Studios in Hyderabad.
  • Varanasi is set for a worldwide theatrical release on April 7, 2027, in over 120 countries, marking the widest global release for any Indian film.

SS Rajamouli has made a career of redefining what Indian cinema can do. Baahubali proved Indian films could compete on a global stage. RRR won an Oscar. Now, with Varanasi, the filmmaker is attempting something no non-English production has done before: shooting a feature film entirely in the 1.43:1 IMAX format — the same ultra-premium format used by Christopher Nolan for Oppenheimer and Interstellar.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=GFCvD76qwPA

What 1.43:1 IMAX Means

Most films released in IMAX are simply "blown up" — standard footage scaled to fit larger screens. Even films marketed as IMAX releases typically use the 1.90:1 widescreen format. Rajamouli's Baahubali and RRR were produced in this wider IMAX format. The 1.43:1 ratio is different — it fills the entire IMAX screen vertically, creating a taller, more immersive frame that has been the exclusive domain of Hollywood's biggest productions.

https://x.com/AuTelugu_Films/status/2084261961009917952

"We make all the films with CinemaScope, and most of them are made in the CinemaScope format," Rajamouli explained at the Globetrotter event in Hyderabad in November 2025, where the film's first look was unveiled. "Many times, the films we watch in IMAX theatres are the films we have made, blown up and scaled up, and branded as IMAX. That is not True IMAX."

A Rs 1,000 Crore Bet on Indian Mythology

Varanasi follows a Shiva devotee, played by Mahesh Babu, who embarks on a mission to retrieve an ancient cosmic artifact. The journey takes him through multiple historical eras, with a narrative that draws from Hindu mythology, including sequences inspired by the Ramayana featuring Rama and Kumbhakarna. Writer V Vijayendra Prasad, Rajamouli's father and longtime collaborator, has described a captivating 30-minute sequence centred on this mythological battle.

"It's about the experience. It's the experience that will transport you through unimaginably big, gigantic worlds, not just in terms of scale, but in terms of emotions as well."

— SS Rajamouli, Director

The production has assembled Hollywood-grade infrastructure. Three international VFX studios — Cinesite (Black Panther: Wakanda Forever), Trixter (Predator: Badlands), and Assemblage Entertainment — are delivering visual effects. A state-of-the-art motion capture facility, built at Nagarjuna's Annapurna Studios in partnership with Hollywood's Animatrik Film Design (Avengers: Endgame, Spider-Man: No Way Home), uses 26-megapixel Vicon Valkyrie cameras and Unreal Engine for real-time visualisation.

A Star-Studded Global Cast

Telugu superstar Mahesh Babu leads the film in what is being positioned as his biggest project to date. Priyanka Chopra Jonas returns to Indian cinema after several Hollywood projects, playing a character named Mandakini. Prithviraj Sukumaran rounds out the lead cast. The soundtrack is composed by M.M. Keeravani, Rajamouli's long-time musical collaborator and the Oscar-winning composer behind RRR's "Naatu Naatu."

The Widest Indian Release Ever

Varanasi is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on April 7, 2027, in standard, Dolby Cinema, and IMAX formats. Shot in Telugu, it will also release in dubbed Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam, and Kannada versions. The film will release in more than 120 countries — the widest global footprint for any Indian production.

For Indian diaspora audiences worldwide, this marks a new milestone: an Indian film designed from the ground up to deliver the same premium theatrical experience as Hollywood's biggest spectacles. Whether Varanasi delivers on that promise will become clear in April 2027.
